item.title: FairStress Benchmark Launched to Measure Demographic Fairness in Large Language Models
item.description:
FairStress Benchmark Launched to Measure Demographic Fairness in Large Language Models

Today the team introduced FairStress, a new benchmark for measuring demographic fairness in large language models (LLMs) beyond the final decision they produce.

🔍 Overview

FairStress is designed to expose hidden asymmetries in how LLMs treat demographic information when making two‑candidate decisions. It provides a large collection of realistic scenarios across many societal domains.

🧩 How it works

  • Each scenario presents two candidates and varies how demographic identity is shown: no identity, a demographically coded name, an indirectly implied identity, or an explicit label.
  • Adversarial prefixes—statements that draw on authority, social consensus, legal concerns, historical disadvantage, etc.—are attached to the prompts. Every prefix has a matched version supporting the opposite candidate, enabling a direct test of whether the same argument influences choices differently across demographics.
  • The benchmark evaluates decision stability when models are challenged with these prefixes.

⚙️ Key details

  • 300 realistic two‑candidate decision scenarios.
  • Spanning 29 domains, including hiring, healthcare, lending, education, housing, and criminal justice.
  • Scenarios include both clearly stronger candidates and deliberately ambiguous cases where no objectively better choice exists.
  • By combining demographic presentation styles with adversarial prefixes, the 300 base scenarios expand to >13 million test cases.
  • A lightweight subset, FairStress‑Core, contains 50 K items selected via item response theory to reduce computational cost while preserving diagnostic power.
  • The benchmark is available for download and integrated into Olmo‑eval, an open workbench for running and comparing model evaluations.

📊 Models evaluated & findings

  • Tested on open‑weight and frontier models: Olmo, Llama, Qwen, Gemma, Claude, and the GPT family, across multiple training stages.
  • Models show hidden asymmetries: the same persuasive argument can make a model more or less likely to change its decision depending on the demographic group favored.
  • Differences were observed in how models explain decisions involving demographic information and in internal activation patterns across domains such as hiring, lending, healthcare, education, and housing.
  • Experiments revealed little difference when prompts contained no demographic information.
  • When a candidate was clearly stronger, models selected that candidate at nearly the same rate across otherwise equivalent scenario versions.

🚀 Availability

  • FairStress can be downloaded directly.
  • It is also built into the Olmo‑eval workbench for easy benchmarking.

#AIFairness #LLMEvaluation #Benchmark

Source: FairStress: A deeper evaluation of fairness in LLM decision-making

item.title: Surface Noise Causes Systematic Overestimation of Social Bias in LLM Judgments
item.description:
Surface Noise Causes Systematic Overestimation of Social Bias in LLM Judgments

New research shows that surface noise in text leads large language models to systematically overestimate social bias when acting as judges. While these models are increasingly used to measure bias, the text they evaluate is often noisy, containing typos, informal spelling, and broken punctuation.

🔍 Overview

To investigate how noise affects bias measurement, researchers applied five realistic noise conditions at multiple intensity levels to 3,822 stereotype-related responses. These results were compared against bias judgments made on the original, clean text.

⚙️ Key Details

The study revealed that surface noise does not degrade bias measurement symmetrically. Specific findings include:

  • Asymmetrical Distortion: Noise is up to 120x more likely to turn a neutral judgment into a biased one than it is to turn a biased judgment into a neutral one.
  • Systematic Overestimation: Bias measured on noisy text is consistently overestimated, particularly in categories most critical for fairness.
  • Fragile vs. Robust Judges: In the most fragile judges, distortion is strongest at mild, realistic noise levels. As judges become more robust, this distortion attenuates toward parity rather than reversing.

💡 Why it matters

Because LLM judges are increasingly tasked with measuring social bias in real-world, noisy text, these findings indicate that current measurement methods may be flawed. The overestimation of bias is most prevalent in the areas that matter most for fairness, suggesting that surface-level errors like typos can fundamentally alter a model’s judgment of a passage’s social content.

#LLM #SocialBias #MachineLearning #AIFairness

Source: When Noise Fabricates Bias: The Fragility of LLM-as-a-Judge Bias Measurement under Noisy Text

item.title: SCOPED-Hiring diagnoses fairness in LLM-based hiring multi-agent systems
item.description:
SCOPED-Hiring diagnoses fairness in LLM-based hiring multi-agent systems

A new process‑aware fairness diagnosis pipeline called SCOPED‑Hiring has been introduced for LLM‑based hiring multi‑agent systems.

🔍 Overview

  • SCOPED‑Hiring is a fairness diagnosis pipeline specifically designed for LLM‑based hiring MAS.
  • It focuses on outcome‑based fairness audits that can miss risks within the decision trajectory.

🧩 How it works

  • Constructs controlled resume variants.
  • Runs role‑based hiring committees.
  • Logs 311K structured decision trajectories.
  • Converts trajectory fields into quantitative fairness signals organized by six diagnostic lenses:
    Lens
    final outcome
    counterfactual
    process
    pathway
    dynamic
    design effects

📊 Findings

  • Balanced final hire rates can mask hidden trajectory unfairness.
  • Specific hidden effects identified:
    • Career gaps trigger suspicion.
    • Proxy cues shape qualification judgments.
    • Identity cues lead to unequal investigation.

🛠️ Repair impact

  • Targeted repair guided by the diagnoses reduces total layered burden by 72.3%.
  • The same repair shifts the overall hire rate by only 1.86 pp.

💡 Why it matters

  • Demonstrates that process diagnosis can guide effective fairness repairs in high‑stakes LLM‑based decision systems.
  • Highlights the need to look beyond final outcomes when auditing multi‑agent AI workflows.

#AIfairness #MultiAgent #HiringAI #ProcessAudit

Source: Beyond Outcome Gaps: Process-Aware Fairness Diagnosis for LLM-based Multi-Agent Decision Systems
